papers.title: Game-Theoretic Lens on LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.finding: A survey organized around players, strategies, payoffs and information. It distinguishes partial observability from full information and discusses incentives, communication and evaluation.
papers.application_inference: Preserve separate buyer objectives, legal actions and uncertain supplier beliefs. Match public case information before comparing environments; never give the buyer a simulated seller's hidden floor.
papers.limitation: This is a taxonomy and survey, not a tested Tacto negotiation policy or evidence that a particular prompt improves arena scores.

papers.title: Device-Native Autonomous Agents for Privacy-Preserving Negotiations
papers.finding: Proposes local state, explainable memory, distilled world models, privacy proofs, selective offloading and a simulation critic. Reports controlled insurance and B2B experiments.
papers.application_inference: Keep deterministic validation and concise decision diagnostics outside the prompt. Preserve executable offers and constraints in local fixtures. Treat simulated responses as hypotheses.
papers.limitation: Its limitations acknowledge controlled scenarios, rational-counterparty assumptions and behavioral privacy leakage. Its success and latency figures do not predict Claude/Tacto performance. Our Claude backend is remote; we do not claim device-native privacy or cryptographic verification.

papers.title: GameTalk: Training LLMs for Strategic Conversation
papers.finding: Adapts GRPO, DPO and STaR using full-conversation outcomes. Separates opponent prediction, action quality given beliefs and conversational influence. DPO is strongest on the reported bargaining game; GRPO has higher rock-paper-scissors reward.
papers.application_inference: Evaluate complete negotiations and validate forecasts against observed replies rather than rewarding plausible sounding planning. Retain failures and per-case regressions.
papers.limitation: Experiments use two-player games and a fixed LLM opponent. The authors report a disconnect between improved outcomes and accurate opponent modeling. Reading the paper does not fine-tune our Claude model; its metrics require information unavailable from the hosted opponent.

decision: No tactic or prompt changes for this single diagnostic hosted run. Original prompt plus four reliability fixes; experimental lookahead gate remains closed.

local_parity.confirmed: The upstream kit explicitly withholds hosted suppliers; its script teaches the API contract.
